context.body: Selected for the reader trail because “Darkness, a loud cry, a torn veil, opened tombs, and watching women” preserves a distinct core source unit within death witness.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Darkness, a loud psalmic cry, bystander response, another cry, death, torn veil, earthquake, opened tombs, and witness reactions follow.
observations.label: Darkness, a loud cry, a torn veil, opened tombs, and watching women: textual observation

observations.body: Jesus addresses God; nearby hearers interpret the words as a call for Elijah.
observations.label: Darkness, a loud cry, a torn veil, opened tombs, and watching women: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: The centurion and guards fear, while named women watch from a distance.
observations.label: Relationships named in Matthew 27:45–56

payload.posture: Read Matthew 27:45–56 as its own death, signs, and witnesses crucifixion setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The death scene joins immediate signs with tomb material whose narrated continuation is explicitly later.
payload.title: Darkness, a loud cry, a torn veil, opened tombs, and watching women
